---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- Python 3.12 (pinned in `.python-version` and enforced by `pyproject.toml`)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management
- Roughly 4 GB of free disk space for the environment
- Git, if you clone rather than download a zip

The analysis itself needs considerably more disk space for the data, see [Data](data.qmd).

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/holukas/ms-forests-vpd.git
cd ms-forests-vpd
uv sync
```

`uv sync` reads `uv.lock` and creates `.venv` with the exact package versions used for
the manuscript. If uv is not on your machine yet:

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

uv downloads Python 3.12 itself if the system does not have it, so no separate Python
install is needed.

## Running scripts

Scripts import from `src/`, which `uv sync` installs into the environment in editable
mode. Paths are resolved from the repository root, not from the working directory, so
scripts can be started from anywhere:

```bash
uv run python scripts/30_shap/31_shap.py
```

## Packages

Direct dependencies, declared in `pyproject.toml`:

| Package | Version | Used for |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `diive` | 0.91.0 | Parquet I/O, FLUXNET file reading, grid aggregation, heatmaps, ET from LE |
| `pandas` | >=3.0, <4.0 | Data handling |
| `numpy` | >=2.2.4, <2.5 | Numerics |
| `scipy` | >=1.15, <2.0 | Z-scores, nearest-neighbour search, statistics |
| `matplotlib` | >=3.10, <4.0 | All figures |
| `scikit-learn` | >=1.6.1, <2.0 | Cross-validation, metrics, hyperparameter search |
| `xgboost` | >=3.0, <4.0 | Gradient-boosted regression models |
| `shap` | >=0.50, <1.0 | SHAP values via `TreeExplainer` |
| `pyale` | >=1.2, <2.0 | Accumulated Local Effects curves |
| `geopandas` | >=1.1.1, <2.0 | Site map |
| `pyyaml` | >=6.0.2, <7.0 | Reading `config/settings.yaml` |
| `openpyxl` | >=3.1.5, <4.0 | Writing the Extended Data table |

The numpy upper bound comes from numba, which shap pulls in and which does not yet
support numpy 2.5. Without the bound the resolver picks a numba release that fails to
build on Python 3.12.

Transitive versions are pinned in `uv.lock`.

### Optional: ERA5 downloads

Scripts `16a` to `16d` re-download ERA5 climate normals and need extra packages plus
personal credentials:

```bash
uv sync --extra era5
```

This is only needed to rebuild the ERA5 climate normals from scratch. The rest of the
pipeline reads the aggregated result. See [Data](data.qmd) for the credentials.

### Optional: development tools

```bash
uv sync --group dev
```

Adds JupyterLab, pytest, Quarto and ghp-import. The `quarto-cli` package ships the
Quarto binary, so no separate system install is needed.

## Building these docs

The documentation is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website under `docs/`. Notebooks
and code blocks are not executed at render time, so no data folder is required.

Live preview with reload on save:

```powershell
.\preview_docs.ps1
```

Build once into `docs/_site/`:

```powershell
.\preview_docs.ps1 -Render
```

`-Port` and `-NoBrowser` are passed through to Quarto. The script uses the Quarto binary
from `.venv` and falls back to one on `PATH`. `Get-Help .\preview_docs.ps1 -Examples`
shows the usage.

Outside Windows, call Quarto directly:

```bash
uv run quarto preview docs
uv run quarto render docs
```

The published version is built by GitHub Actions on every push to `main`, which needs
Pages enabled on the repository. To push a build by hand instead:

```powershell
.\preview_docs.ps1 -Render
uv run ghp-import -n -p -f docs/_site
```
